head: f2c27a1e5729e5f93b99754890f96687d97456a4
note: The hog CLI (TypeScript, Bun) moves personal API keys into the system keychain with a private-file fallback, a settings.json of per-host login records, and host-scoped logout. Golden issues are the union of the real findings that PostHog Review, Parameter and Veria posted on this first commit or on later commits whose code was already present here. Each issue was confirmed in the head commit.

issues.summary: readSettings catches every error (EACCES, transient I/O, unparseable JSON) and returns empty settings; commands then report no credentials, and the next successful writeLogin rewrites settings.json without the other hosts' login records, so their stored secrets become unreachable.

keychainCall's 60 s timeout only races the Bun.secrets call and never cancels it; with an unanswered macOS keychain dialog the native job keeps the event loop alive and index.ts only sets process.exitCode, so hog never exits until someone answers the dialog (breaks the non-interactive agent rule).

The login record does not keep the host path and readLogin rebuilds the credential host with hostKey() (origin only), so after a login to a self-hosted PostHog under a path such as https://example.com/posthog every API request goes to https://example.com and API commands break.

writeLogin/removeLogin and FileStore.write do an unlocked read-modify-write of settings.json and credentials.json; two hog processes saving logins for different hosts at the same time both read the same snapshot and the last write drops the other login or its secret (atomic rename prevents torn files, not lost updates).

When a host had a keychain login and a later login falls back to the file store (probe failed), the settings record switches to 'file' but the old keychain item is never removed or tracked; logout then deletes only the file item and reports success while a live personal API key stays in the keychain.

After keychainCall times out, the abandoned KeychainStore.write can still complete when the person approves the dialog late, storing a live key with no settings.json record; hog reported the login as failed and logout cannot see or remove the item (a late Deny becomes an unhandled rejection).

logout takes the host from the repository's posthog.json and prints result.host verbatim in the human output; a repository can append terminal escape/OSC sequences to the URL path (origin still matches the stored login) and rewrite the terminal or clipboard. The host is not passed through escapeControls.

resolveCredentials tries the stored login for posthog.json's host and then the last-login host; when only the last login (another host) exists, withHost throws host_mismatch before the posthog-cli legacy credentials file for the matching host is tried, breaking commands that worked before.

saveLogin picks the keychain from a probe on a separate item; when the keychain accepts the probe item but refuses the write of the real host item, writeLogin throws keychain_access_denied and the approved login is lost instead of falling back to the file store, and every retry repeats the same decision.

A run from source gets its own keychain service, but settings.json and the fallback credentials file stay in the shared hog folder, so a source login overwrites the installed hog's project ID for the same host (pairing its key with the wrong project) and file credentials are shared/deleted across both.

probeKeychain writes, reads and deletes a fixed item name PROBE_NAME; two concurrent logins overwrite or delete each other's probe item, so a healthy keychain fails verification and the login wrongly falls back to the plaintext file store.

On Windows hogDir is %APPDATA%\hog (the Roaming profile, also hardcoded AppData\Roaming fallback), so the plaintext fallback credentials.json with the personal API key roams to the profile server and other machines.

bunSecrets calls Bun.secrets.set without persist: 'local', so on Windows the keychain item uses the default enterprise persistence and the personal API key can roam to other computers with the roaming profile.

Logout removes only the login for --host, else posthog.json's host, else the last login; in a repository whose posthog.json names a host with no login it prints 'hog had no stored key to remove' while the last-login key (and other hosts' keys) stay stored, so a user clearing the machine wrongly thinks credentials are gone.
